questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Opportunities for interesting field courses!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro week with lots of social events and info sessions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Found housing within a week - however, the selection was not great since Perth was and still is in a huge Housing Crisis (meaning that most apartments are far away from the city centre and completely over priced). I managed to get an ok deal with a shared apartment close to UWA. I can recommend using the  premium version of
flatmates.com.au
.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Come well before semester start so you can afford being critical regarding the housing options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Accomodation offered by UWA is quite expensive, which is why opted for an off-campus option.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only minus was that we could only change our courses within the first week, which is not enough time to really get an impression of the courses. In retrospective I would have swopped one course in order to avoid too much time-consuming lab work.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I cannot remember the details - but it was pretty straightforward. One just had to follow the instructions provied by e-mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UWA offers helping sessions regarding course registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got into all the courses that I wanted. UWA staff was in general quite helpful and responded quickly, if there were problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the course descriptions carfeully and contact the coordinator, if in doubt.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really happy about my courses and learnt a lot!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Out of four courses, three were pretty much what I expected on the basis of their course descriptions. However, one courses turned out to be a Master Course and included advanced programming R - which was not mentioned on the website and which I found very challenging since I've never used it before. I was lucky that that the course supervisor was super patient and provided good exercises. In general, I also underestimated the additional work load connected to field work and lab sessions.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much more flexible. All lectures were available online. Good mix between independent work and group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental Assessment.
Soil Science.
Chemistry - Structure and Reactivity.
GIS Applications.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend the courses infividually. However, combined their work load was too high since they all included additional field work and/or lab work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Extra costs for spontanoeus rips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing costs were much higher than expected due to the current Housing Crisis in Perth. I was lucky only having to pay 250 AUSD per month - most of my peers had to pay at least 350 AUSD or even more, if they opted for an campus accomodation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many! Wanted to stay sponatenous and opted only for the UWA Outdoor Club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can definetely recommend the UWA Outdoor Club - loved especially the climbing! Met most of my friends through there that then also took me surfing and hiking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Wine tasting, trekking and biking can be done in the Perth surrounding. Otherwise there are great road trip destinations especially in the South.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy - Aussies are quite chatty and easy-going.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The field trips and most of my lab wok was done in groups, which was nice so I could get to know some of my Aussie peer students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Aussies are much more open and welcoming than Danes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I felt like that everybody in Perth was pretty relaxed and welcoming. Lots of sponatneous surfing and BBQs.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Wetsuit. Climbing gear. And enough money for spontanoeus trips.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend science students to choose a good balance of the courses. I spent many more hours at uni than my fellow exchange students since I had so much lab work (which was super interesting, but combined just too much.)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making sense of the data collected in the field.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The work load from uni plus my side job was quite stressful in the long run. I would recommend future exchange students to make sure that they have enough financial assets in order to have a more relaxed stay and more opportunities to join longer road trips with friends. Australia is cheaper than DK - but still relatively expensive and not affordable with only SU.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can definetely recommend UWA to students who study natural science!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
